newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Gasunie turnover grows 10 pct in cold 1996.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Gasunie turnover grows 10 pct in cold 1996.

text.p: Dutch gas distributor Gasunie said on Tuesday heavy gas demand in winter months had led to a 10 percent rise in turnover in 1996 to 18.7 billion guilders.
Gasunie's total gas supply rose by 12.9 percent to 93.8 billion cubic metres (bcm). Domestic supply was up 7.2 percent to 47.9 bcm. Exports rose 19.5 percent to 45.9 bcm.

The average selling price was 20 guilder cents per cubic metre. This was half a cent lower than in 1995, but actually represented a rise as the 1995 price included non-recurring retrospective payments under renegotiated export contracts.
The rise, however, was not as sharp as that of oil prices. Although the price of gas is linked to that of fuel oil and gas oil, there is a time-lag.

On the domestic front, Gasunie said competive pressures were mounting. Customers were increasingly interested in gas from Britain which should be available in 1998 when the Interconnector pipeline comes into operation.

"(Gasunie) is confident that its reputation for reliability gives it a competitive edge, but it is no longer realistic...to expect to defend its current market position without some erosion," Gasunie said in a statement.
It said it aimed to compensate for lost domestic share by increasing exports, particularly in central and eastern Europe.

This year, Gasunie expects to supply around 86 bcm of gas based on normal temperatures and slight structural growth in the domestic market. Higher prices should lead to a turnover of around 19 billion guilders.
Over the next 25 years, Gasunie expects domestic sales to total 1,250 bcm and exports to total 790 bcm, which includes 240 bcm of additional exports approved by the Dutch government last year.

Gasunie estimates total gas reserves of about 2,470 bcm and estimated total demand of 2,040 bcm over the next 25 years, leaving reserves of 430 bcm available at the end of that period, enough to meet Dutch gas demand for almost 10 years more.
Gasunie is owned 50 percent by the Dutch state and 25 percent each by Royal Dutch/Shell and Exxon Corp unit Esso.
